items.problem: A C# UWP app that ProjectReferences a native WinRT component (a .vcxproj C++/CX or C++/WinRT helper) has no migration guidance. The agent spent ~9 turns manually browsing the solution and hand-writing a PE-header parser to prove the OpenCVBridge DLL was AppContainer-flagged before deciding to replace it.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines ~1486-2012: reads ..\shared\OpenCVBridge, lists OpenCVBridge.winmd/.dll, PE-parses DllCharacteristics=0x1160 -> IsAppContainer:True (turn 22), then 'OpenCVBridge.dll is AppContainer-flagged so I'll use OpenCvSharp4 instead' (turn 24). build-events.jsonl shows the ProjectReference at the UWP csproj: <ProjectReference Include="..\shared\OpenCVBridge\OpenCVBridge.vcxproj">.
items.skill_search: grepped SKILL.md, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, and scripts/*.ps1|*.json for 'ProjectReference', 'vcxproj', 'winmd', 'native', 'C++', 'AppContainer', 'component'
items.root_cause: The skill covers migrating C# source and reconciling the csproj's PackageReferences, but never addresses a ProjectReference to a native WinRT component. The bootstrap preserves the UWP .csproj at .uwp-source/ but does not parse it for native project references, so the dependency is never surfaced.
items.proposed_fix: (1) Tier 1: in Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1, scan the preserved UWP .csproj(s) for <ProjectReference> pointing at a native project (.vcxproj) and print a prominent warning in the BOOTSTRAP COMPLETE block referencing a new pattern anchor. (2) Tier 3: add a 'Native WinRT component ProjectReference' section to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md (anchor native-component) stating the AppContainer-load rule and the rebuild-or-replace decision.
items.generalizes: UWP apps frequently ProjectReference a native C++ acceleration/helper component (Windows-universal-samples ship shared native helpers such as OpenCVBridge, and many production UWP apps use C++/WinRT interop components). Any such app will hit the same AppContainer-load wall on WinUI 3 desktop, so a general rebuild-or-replace pattern applies broadly.
